svg.title: Every Page Links Out
svg.desc: Sketch from high above, looking down at an angle over open water: a large island in the middle, its top hatched, with a page standing upright on it, is joined by plank bridges to four smaller islands. On the four islands, in turn, are a small table ruled as a grid, an upright card with a circle on it, a closed book, and a thread circle. Each island is a page on the site. The open water between them is the problem: pages written one at a time drift apart, and a reader who lands on one never reaches the rest. The hatched middle island is any single page, the focus. Its bridges are its links, the solution: the grid is the table, the card is a pattern the page introduces or applies, the book is the sources it draws on, and the thread circle is the other pieces in its thread. The metaphor: the site as an archipelago. A page with no bridges is an island in the bad sense.
